Российская лингвистическая экспедиция в Кот-д'Ивуар и орфографические реформы в южных языках манде [Russian linguistic field trips to Cote d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. Кунсткамера (Kunstkamera) 2019, No. 4(6): 107-121.

5343.idn: Name in the source: гоо (Goo); family in the source: южные языки манде (South Mande group); closest relative тура (Tura); formerly considered a dialect intermediate between дан (Dan) and тура

tn.quote: Все эти языки политонические: половина из них (уан, муан, гуро, нген, бен) имеет по 3 уровневых тона (трехтоновый также и язык мано, распространенный в Гвинее и Либерии), половина (западный дан, кла-дан, гоо, тура, яурэ, гбан) — по 4; восточный дан имеет 5 уровневых тонов, при этом гуро, бен, западный и восточный дан, гбан имеют также модулированные тоны. Во всех этих языках тоны несут большую функциональную нагрузку и служат не только для лексического контраста, но и для выражения многочисленных грамматических значений.
tn.translation: All these languages are polytonic: half of them (Wan, Mwan, Guro, Ngen, Beng) have 3 level tones each (Mano, spoken in Guinea and Liberia, is also three-tone), half (Western Dan, Kla-Dan, Goo, Tura, Yaoure, Gban) have 4 each; Eastern Dan has 5 level tones, while Guro, Beng, Western and Eastern Dan and Gban also have modulated (contour) tones. In all these languages tones carry a heavy functional load and serve not only for lexical contrast but also to express numerous grammatical meanings.
tn.cite: Выдрин, В. Ф. [Vydrin, Valentin F.]. 2019. Российская лингвистическая экспедиция в Кот-д'Ивуар и орфографические реформы в южных языках манде [Russian linguistic field trips to Cote d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. Кунсткамера (Kunstkamera) 2019, No. 4(6): 107-121.
tn.locator: p. 108, 'Введение'
tn.note: Survey: Goo has 4 level tones, no contour tones (not among languages listed with modulated tones), heavy lexical+grammatical load; labels not given (Aplonova 2019: extra-high, high, low, extra-low).

tn.quote: The Qimen Hui Chinese dialect has 6 tonal categories, namely yin-ping, yang-ping, shang, yin-qu, yang-qu and yin-ru. ... In summary, Qimen tones are transcribed as follows: yin-ping /22/, yang-ping /55/, shang /41/, yin-qu /23/, yang-qu /33/, and yin-ru /25/. ... it is tenable to conclude that the Qimen dialect obviously has a three-way distinction of level tones. ... In summary, Qimen distinguishes three level tones, two rising tones, and one falling tone.

evidence_works.work: Lu 2018, Aspects of the grammar of Tunxi Hui: a transitional Sinitic language (PhD thesis, University of Hong Kong: pp. 47-56, 123-125)
evidence_works.detail: Reference grammar of Tunxi Hui, a second Hui variety beside the entry's Qimen. Data: recorded daily conversations between native speakers plus linguistic elicitation (p. 28), consultants native-born Tunxi District residents over fifty (p. 31). Ch. 2.5 Tones: 'Tunxi Hui has six citation tones and a very complex tone sandhi system' (p. 47); sandhi rule (i): 'it is exclusively the preceding tone in a disyllabic word or phrase that will change its tone value, a pattern known as right-dominant tone sandhi' (p. 49); 'Neutral tones in Tunxi Hui, while they may be found, are not as evident or as common as in Mandarin. They only occur in functional words' (p. 54). The word 'stress' occurs once in the thesis, in 5.1.1 on strong vs weak personal-pronoun forms: strong forms 'are prosodically prominent, in terms of not only volume and length, but also and pitch and timbre' (p. 123) and 'the unstressed weak forms are' ungrammatical in contrastive constructions (p. 125); this is phrasal strong/weak-form prominence of pronouns, not a word-stress rule. No statement on lexical stress or its absence.

5346.idn: Name in the source: Izere (Ibor dialect; 'the Izere language of Fobur'); Jarawan Dutse (Hausa name); Afizere; Izarek; dialects Ibor, Isum, Iganang, Ifudere, Ikyo; family in the source: part of the Plateau language family (Benue-Congo, Greenberg 1963)…; the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones. ... There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL). Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened ... As such these synchronic occurrences are probably transitional and Izere can be regarded as having an underlying three-height system. Tones are marked as follows; HIGH acute accent above the syllable kú to die MID unmarked fa to count LOW grave accent over the syllable mì I ...
tn.cite: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Bulus Kaze. n.d. [draft dated 2006]. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur: introduction (20 pp.), section 4.1 'Izere phonology'
tn.locator: sec. 4.1 'Izere phonology', pp. 9-10
tn.note: Five tones: high, mid, low, rising (LM), falling (HL); contours only in loans, bird names, shortened VV, so underlyingly three heights per the authors. Affixes bear varied tones. Nothing on stress.

5349.idn: Name in the source: kenga; family in the source: langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes > branche « occidentale » > rameau « sara » (with mbay, ngambay, kaba-na, bagiro)

tn.quote: les systèmes tonals de ces langues — qui distinguent, selon les cas, trois ou quatre registres — s'expliquent en effet comme la résultante d'un système « occidental commun » de trois registres ... Les caractéristiques tonales — communes au bagiro, au mbay, au ngambay, au kenga et au kaba-na — sur lesquelles on fonde la spécificité des langues sara sont les suivantes20: ... — choix exclusif, pour certains termes, de la seconde variante du scheme nominal « occidental commun » * MM ~ * HB (bagiro et mbay HH; ngam- bay H(M); kenga et kaba-na HB)

The tonal characteristics — common to Bagiro, Mbay, Ngambay, Kenga and Kaba-na — on which the specificity of the Sara languages is founded are the following: ... — exclusive choice, for certain terms, of the second variant of the 'common western' nominal scheme *MM ~ *HB (Bagiro and Mbay HH; Ngambay H(M); Kenga and Kaba-na HB)

refs.ref: Ōtake Masami (大竹昌巳). 2024. 契丹語の音調 [Pitch Realization in Khitan]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu: Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 165: 85-110. DOI 10.11435/gengo.165.0_85

5351.loc: p. 105 (sec. 4.1) and p. 106 (sec. 4.2); English abstract p. 110 restates: 'Khitan was a phrase language with an L tone at the left edge and an H tone at the right edge of every word or phrase'
5351.idn: Name in the source: 契丹語 (Khitan); family in the source: マクロモンゴル語族 (Macro-Mongolic family); モンゴル諸語と系統関係を有する 'related to the Mongolic languages' but not their direct ancestor

tn.quote: したがってこのことは，遼代初期の契丹語が，初頭音節のピッチが低く，末音節のピッチが高いという一定の音調形式を有したことを意味していると解釈することができる。... モンゴル諸語は語彙声調（lexical tone）も語彙強勢（lexical stress）も持たないが，韻律語もしくはアクセント句（accentual phrase）等，後語彙的な韻律単位の境界で実現する句音調（phrasal tone）をもつ phrase language（Féry 2010, 2017: 269–281）に分類される言語であり，... 契丹語が現代モンゴル諸語のような phrase language であったことを物語っている。... 契丹語音訳語彙の陰陽調字の分布は，この言語が左端を L 音調で明示し，緩やかなピッチの上昇ののち右端を H 音調で明示するという，左右両端の 2 つの境界画定機能をもつ音調によって形づくられるピッチ曲線を有したことを示すと解釈できる。
tn.translation: This can therefore be interpreted to mean that early-Liao Khitan had a fixed pitch pattern in which the initial syllable was low-pitched and the final syllable high-pitched. ... The Mongolic languages have neither lexical tone nor lexical stress, but are classified as phrase languages (Féry 2010, 2017: 269-281) having phrasal tones realised at the boundaries of post-lexical prosodic units such as the prosodic word or accentual phrase, ... [this] tells us that Khitan was a phrase language like the modern Mongolic languages. ...
tn.cite: Ōtake Masami (大竹昌巳). 2024. 契丹語の音調 [Pitch Realization in Khitan]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu: Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 165: 85-110. DOI 10.11435/gengo.165.0_85
tn.locator: p. 105 (sec. 4.1) and p. 106 (sec. 4.2); English abstract p. 110 restates: 'Khitan was a phrase language with an L tone at the left edge and an H tone at the right edge of every word or phrase'
tn.note: Extinct Khitan reconstructed as a phrase language: no lexical tone; every word/phrase low at left edge (L boundary tone), high at right (H). Evidence: tone categories of Chinese transcription chars.

5351.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

refs.ref: Давыдов, А. В. [Davydov, Artem V.]. 2017. Манден диалекты Гвинеи [Manden dialects of Guinea]. In В. Ф. Выдрин, Ю. В. Мазурова, А. А. Кибрик & Е. Б. Маркус (eds.), Языки мира: Языки манде, 164-171. Санкт-Петербург: Нестор-История.

5352.loc: p. 170, sec. 6 (tone paragraph); then p. 166, sec. 5 items 1-3
5352.idn: Name in the source: коранко; западный и восточный коранко; санкаран-коранко (transitional idiom between Koranko and Maninka); family in the source: Язык коранко входит в группу моколе, при этом он является частью единого с манден далектного континуума (Mokole group; part of one dialect continuum with Manden)

tn.quote: Большинство идиомов манден имеет две базовые тоновые схемы слов. Так, в манинка-мори выделяются слова с высоким и с низким (восходящим) тоном. Тоновые схемы односложных и многосложных слов совпадают. Тоны могут реализоваться как на одной гласной (bá ‛мать’, bà ‛коза’), так и на двух и более: bóló ‛рука’, mòsò ‛женщина’. ... 1. Манинка. Основные признаки: неинвертированные тоновые схемы ... 2. Конья ... Основные признаки: инвертированные тоновые схемы ... 3. Коранко. Фонологически ближе к манинка, чем к конья, однако имеет большое количество лексических расхождений как одним, так и с другим.
tn.translation: Most Manden idioms have two basic tonal word patterns. Thus in Maninka-Mori words with high and with low (rising) tone are distinguished. The tonal patterns of monosyllabic and polysyllabic words coincide. The tones may be realised on one vowel (bá 'mother', bà 'goat') or on two or more: bóló 'arm', mòsò 'woman'. ... 1. Maninka. Main features: non-inverted tonal patterns ... 2. Konya ... Main features: inverted tonal patterns ... 3. Koranko. Phonologically closer to Maninka than to Konya, but with many lexical divergences from both.
tn.cite: Давыдов, А. В. [Davydov, Artem V.]. 2017. Манден диалекты Гвинеи [Manden dialects of Guinea]. In В. Ф. Выдрин, Ю. В. Мазурова, А. А. Кибрик & Е. Б. Маркус (eds.), Языки мира: Языки манде, 164-171. Санкт-Петербург: Нестор-История.
tn.locator: p. 170, sec. 6 (tone paragraph); then p. 166, sec. 5 items 1-3
tn.note: Two word-level tone classes (high vs low, low realised as rising) stated for Manden idioms generally; Koranko sides with the non-inverted Maninka type; ~70 tone-marked Koranko forms; no stress/TBU.

tn.quote: 4. Tone There are two level tones (High and Low) and two contour tones (High-Low and Low-High). (3) H dúŋə́ 'snake' HL lây 'liver' L dùŋə̀ 'soot' LH lə̌y 'eye' At most, two tones may be assigned to any one vowel of one and two syllable words. tn.quote: In previous work (Fiore 1987; Fransen 1995), Limbum has been described as a tone language with three level tones (H, L, M) and four contour tones (HL, LM, ML, LL). ... (following Fiore 1987 and Fransen 1995, we assume that the syllable is the TBU in Limbum). ... there are three classes of tones in Limbum: level tones which remain level tones in all positions (L, M, H), level tones that alternate with falling contour tones at the end of declarative sentences and wh-questions (L(L), M(L), H(L)), and a rising contour tone (LM).
tn.cite: Gjersøe, Siri, Jude Nformi & Ludger Paschen. 2019. Hybrid falling tones in Limbum. tn.note: 7 tones (H M L; falling HL ML LL; rising LM; HM marginal, fn.1); contours = two tonal root nodes on one syllable, falling ones surface only phrase-finally via floating L%; downstep only generic.

tn.quote: La langue lɔŋto a trois hauteurs tonales: haut, moyen et bas. Il y a aussi deux tons descendants: haut-bas et rarement moyen-bas. En général les sons qui portent les tons sont les voyelles, et parfois /l/ ~ /r/ et les nasales /m/ ~ /n/ et /ŋ/ s'ils sont les seuls sons d'un morphème ou en position finale d'un mot ou morphème. ... En général les tons descendants sont exclusivement prononcés à la fin d'une phrase. ... Donc, toutes les voyelles qui sont sans marque de ton sont prononcées moyens.
tn.translation: The Lɔŋto language has three tone heights: high, mid and low. There are also two falling tones: high-low and, rarely, mid-low. In general the sounds that bear the tones are the vowels, and sometimes /l/ ~ /r/ and the nasals /m/ ~ /n/ and /ŋ/ if they are the only sounds of a morpheme or in final position of a word or morpheme. ... In general the falling tones are pronounced exclusively at the end of a sentence. ... So all vowels without a tone mark are pronounced mid.
tn.cite: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich (avec l'assistance de Illiassou Godje et Bouba Bakary). 2012 [digital edn 2021, 'Dictionnaire lɔŋto ACAD 1.0']. Lexique Lɔ̀ŋtó (~ Voko) - Français. Poli: Lamido de Voko / Comité de Développement du Lamidat de Voko / DFG. 68 pp.
tn.locator: p. 4, section 1.2 'Le ton'
tn.note: Three level tones (H, M, L) plus falling HL and rare ML, the falls only phrase-finally; long vowels written double may carry two different tones; infinitives never begin with L. Nothing on stress.

evidence_works.work: Patman 1991, Tone in the Nugunu verb phrase (SIL Cameroon typescript = Nugunu chapter of Anderson (ed.) Tone in five languages of Cameroon, SIL/UTA PL 102: 22 pp.)
evidence_works.detail: A first-hand tonological description: sec. 1.0 Introduction states 'Nugunu has two phonemic tones, H and L. These may be realized at any number of phonetic pitch levels because of the process of downdrift, in which the pitch of any H tone following a L is lower than the pitch of preceding H tones. Rising, falling, and rising-falling contours are also found, formed by the juxtaposition of two or more dissimilar tones.'. The paper then posits tone rules for the verb phrase (sec. 2.0 ff.). It contains no statement about stress or accent: the only hit for 'accent' is the orthographic note that the paper marks H and L tones with accents. No elicitation procedure or consultant is described.

tn.quote: Le wori est une langue à tons. ... L'impossibilité de trouver sur un monosyllabe une opposition entre trois tons ponctuels dont aucun ne soit le résultat d'une neutralisation nous a fait considérer que le wori est une langue à tons normalement ponctuels, au nombre de deux. Ces deux registres fondamentaux, haut et bas, donnent quatre possibilités distinctives ... ce qui ne doit pas faire conclure à l'existence de 4 tons en wori, mais signifie seulement que la succession des deux tons ponctuels de cette langue dans le cadre d'une même syllabe a valeur distinctive.
tn.translation: Wori is a tone language. ... The impossibility of finding on a monosyllable an opposition between three level tones none of which results from a neutralisation led us to consider Wori a language with normally level tones, two in number. These two basic registers, high and low, give four distinctive possibilities ... which must not lead one to conclude that there are 4 tones in Wori, but means only that the succession of the two level tones of this language within one syllable is distinctive.
tn.cite: Hagège, Claude. 1967. Description phonologique du parler wori (sud-ouest du Cameroun). Journal of West African Languages 4(2): 15-34.
tn.locator: p. 15, II 'Les tons', Introduction (first sentence); p. 17, II 2 Interprétation (rest)
tn.note: Two level tones (high, low) on every vowel and syllabic nasal; HL and LH on one syllable analysed as two morae, not extra tonemes; L is mid before H or between two H (allotones); nothing on stress.

tn.quote: In Para Naga, three distinct tones are present, namely, High, Mid, and Low. High and mid tones are realized with a slight drop in pitch in utterance final position. ... Table 3 presents minimal sets for the three tones. Note that tone has a relatively low functional load; not every syllable can carry all three tones. ... Para Naga has not only lexical but also grammatical tone. ... Para Naga nouns occur with all three tones and do not undergo tone sandhi. ... The monosyllabic verb roots carry only mid or high tone. ... High tone /⁵⁵/ ... Mid tone /³³/ ... Low tone /¹¹/
